Block-I/O pressure observed (8.00% I/O PSI some).
Verdict: block-I/O pressure · severity moderate · I/O confidence high
Evidence: I/O PSI some 8.00% over exact 10s interval (800ms cumulative stalled time); full 2.00% (200ms all-non-idle-task stall)
Device activity candidates (same window only; not mapped to workloads):
  1. sda (8:0) — read/write 8192 / 16384 512-byte sectors; I/O time 500ms; in-flight 2 (medium; same-window activity only)
Process I/O accounting candidates (same window only; not proven causal or device-mapped):
  1. writer [42] — 1.0 KiB read + 8.0 KiB charged write; 0 B cancelled write (medium; same-window accounting only)
Affected workloads: see scoped delay roles; candidates do not map processes to devices or prove harm
Context and limitations:
  I/O PSI alone does not identify affected workloads; scoped delay candidates require separate process evidence and do not map a process to a device or prove harm.
  Diskstats can include layered, virtual, or stacked devices; activity may be represented more than once and is not ownership attribution.
  Process read_bytes, charged write_bytes, cancelled writes, and diskstats do not reveal page-cache hits, writeback timing, or which storage operation caused a stall.
  I/O PSI `full` is a subset of `some`; it is retained as context and never added to the pressure fraction or used to establish pressure.
  Diskstats activity occurred in the same window as I/O PSI pressure; it does not establish a constrained device or a causal device path.
  Process read_bytes or charged write_bytes changed in the same window as I/O PSI pressure; cancelled writes remain separate, and this does not map the process to a device or prove causality.
Timing: requested 10s; I/O PSI measured 10s; diskstats measured 10s; process I/O measured 10s
